objective: Require executable Pydantic coverage for every committed JSON Schema with a runtime producer or consumer, including bidirectional fixture validation and reviewed exemption metadata.
decision_supported: Can the repository fail CI when a runtime-consumed JSON Schema lacks a typed Pydantic model, an example, or a reviewed exemption, while preserving existing public contract semantics?
acceptance: Every committed JSON Schema has exactly one executable coverage entry with a checked-in example and a typed Pydantic model, or an exemption that names an owner, reason and replacement validation.
EmotionIntent and public Schema-shaped WorldState models are available from workbench_contracts without replacing the World Model reducer's internal state representation.
Pose, TaskGraph and WorldEvent have committed examples and are validated through their canonical Pydantic models.
WorldEvent model vocabulary covers every event_type value declared by world_event.schema.json, while existing reducer behavior remains unchanged.

WorldEvent accepts the schema's optional recorded_at and clock_id fields, and schema-required source, payload, model_route, fault_type and oracle_allowed fields can no longer be omitted through Pydantic defaults.
The MCU legacy sent_at schema-only field has named owner, reason and replacement validation metadata, and both JSON Schema and McuFrame reject it in the executable invalid-frame corpus.
Each covered fixture is validated against JSON Schema before Pydantic parsing and the canonical Pydantic JSON serialization is validated against the same Schema.
A newly committed schema without a coverage entry fails the contract validator and a coverage regression test demonstrates that failure.
No interfaces JSON Schema definition, World Model reducer state, firmware, robot control or public MCU Wire V1 encoding is changed.
commands: python3 -m ruff check libs/contracts/workbench_contracts/models.py libs/contracts/workbench_contracts/__init__.py services/agent_runtime/workbench_agent_runtime/planner.py tools/scripts/validate_contracts.py tests/conftest.py tests/unit/test_contract_coverage.py tests/unit/test_contract_strictness.py tests/unit/test_mcu_protocol_contract.py tests/unit/test_policy_validator.py
evidence: Coverage registry output showing all on-disk schemas mapped to examples and typed models with no unreviewed gaps.
Focused coverage tests proving schema-to-model and model-to-schema round trips plus fail-closed detection of an unregistered schema.
Contract validator, contract-focused tests, full test, scenario, context, Ruff and whitespace-check output.
stop_conditions: A schema semantic or public field change is required rather than a coverage/model mapping change.
The internal World Model state would need to be replaced by the public WorldState JSON shape.
MCU Wire V1 encoding, firmware, robot control or a protected runtime boundary must change.
A required modification falls outside allowed_paths.
Task Packet validation reports a changed path outside allowed_paths.
risks_and_fallbacks: The public schemas intentionally remain broader than some strict runtime models; canonical fixture serialization is the compatibility direction and any broader schema vocabulary must be represented by the typed model or an explicit exemption.
The reducer's internal WorldState remains structurally different from the public schema and is not silently substituted for the public contract model.
Required Runtime, World Model and Integration approvals remain a merge condition for contract-facing changes.
